title: Capacitors
examples: What is the difference between a capacitor and a battery?
How does the size of the capacitor affect its charge?
Can you explain the time constant in an RC circuit?

explain.say: Today we explore capacitors, which are components that store electrical energy.
The capacitance, symbol C, is defined as the ratio of the charge stored to the voltage across it.
The unit for capacitance is the farad, which is a measure of how much charge it can hold.

items: One farad is a large unit

explain.say: The energy stored in a capacitor can be calculated using the formula one half C V squared.
In an RC circuit, the charge builds up exponentially over time when connected to a voltage source.
The time constant, tau, in an RC circuit is simply the resistance times the capacitance value.

faq.q: What is the difference between capacitance and resistance?
faq.a: Resistance opposes current flow, while capacitance stores electrical charge. Resistance is measured in ohms, and capacitance in farads.
asks: How are R and C different?

faq.q: Does the dielectric material affect the capacitance?
faq.a: Yes, the material between the plates, called the dielectric, increases the capacitance value. The material must be an insulator.
asks: What is the role of the dielectric?
Can I use any material inside?

faq.q: What does the time constant tau represent?
faq.a: The time constant tau is the time it takes for the capacitor to charge to about sixty-three percent of its maximum voltage. It depends on R and C.
asks: What is the relationship with R and C?

faq.q: How do I calculate the energy stored?
faq.a: You can use the equation one half C V squared. Remember that C is capacitance and V is voltage.

faq.q: Does the capacitor discharge in the same way it charges?
faq.a: Yes, the discharge process follows the same exponential decay curve as the charging process. The time constant remains the same.
asks: Does it follow the same curve?

facts: Capacitance is measured in farads, symbolized by F.
The energy stored is proportional to the square of the voltage.
In an RC circuit, the time constant tau equals R times C.
A dielectric material is an electrical insulator used between capacitor plates.

quiz.say: If you double the capacitance while keeping voltage constant, how does the stored energy change?
quiz.why: Since energy is directly proportional to capacitance when voltage is constant, doubling C doubles E.

wrong.0: This suggests an inverse relationship that does not exist here.
wrong.2: This confuses the relationship with voltage, which is squared in the formula.
wrong.3: The energy stored clearly depends on the capacitance value.

quiz.say: What is the formula for the time constant tau in an RC circuit?
quiz.why: The time constant is defined as the product of the resistance and the capacitance.

wrong.1: This would be incorrect for determining the time constant.
wrong.2: The relationship is a simple product, not a power.
wrong.3: Adding the units does not yield the correct time unit.

quiz.say: If a capacitor is connected to a circuit with a resistance of ten ohms and a capacitance of one farad, what is the time constant?
quiz.why: The time constant is R multiplied by C, so ten ohms times one farad equals ten seconds.

wrong.1: This incorrectly divides the values instead of multiplying them.
wrong.2: This forgets to multiply by the resistance value.
wrong.3: This incorrectly squares the resistance value.
